Some 35 metres north-east there was a mini roundabout in January 2013, and about 45 metres north, parking called “B&Q”, from that same January. The footway is nameless, and heading for an end.
v16-2acd812463d76cbe.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Dirt underfoot on a nameless footway. “Beckenham Crematorium” lies to the north-west.
Right where you stand, the map marks a point with a note to it: “County border 1889-1965. Now a district border.” You are standing on the line.

Beside you to the north-west, another point, saying only “Elmend Brook”, and to the north a wood. All of it falls within “South Norwood Country Park”. A brook, a border, a crematorium, each at the edge of the next.
v16-2acdad4a21eff1f3.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Chipstead Valley Road, between Woodcote Grove Road and Portnalls Road. Pavement on both hands, lamps at night, 30 mph.
Beside you to the north, a bus stop. It is named “Portnalls Road”, and carries the reference “55618”. Beside it, also to the north, a point the map gives no word for.
The road is thick here. I count from the stop and come unstuck somewhere along, then pick the count back up and carry on.
On Chipstead Valley Road, at a stop that answers to Portnalls Road.
v16-2ad9da1fc684b943.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Paving stones at the end of an unnamed footway, lit at night. Plenty else is about; I will not tally it.
A residential area to the west, a commercial area to the south-west. Beside you to the east, a crossing, with tactile paving. Beside you to the north-west, a hairdresser at George Street.
The hairdresser has a name of its own, and the name is “Jackson's Grooming Room”.
v16-2addd07a93d5e0d9.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: A path with no name, dirt underfoot, and houses off to the north-east. All around lies a nature reserve, “Hutchinson's Bank”.

Beside you to the north-west, they say, a magpie was seen in May 2021. The map has no magpie. It has the reserve, and the path through it, and the houses beyond. I began to tally what else is here and the figure went from me somewhere past the reserve; I take it up again from the path.
A magpie in May 2021, by someone's word; “Hutchinson's Bank”, by the map's.
v16-2aeb1dbb205676fd.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: A residential road with no name, closed at a dead end and open to Sanderstead Road. The map puts you inside the allotments, a railway area and a residential area both to the west.
Beside you on that side, the “Brighton Main Line”, run by Network Rail, reference “VTB2”. A few steps further west, the map gives it again, the same name, the same reference.
I count them, then lose the count, then find it. The line is drawn again beside itself; the allotments hold their name: “South Croydon Allotments”.
v16-2af1eee360bc7884.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Stevens Place, 20 mph. Stevens Place holds more than I shall pass on; I keep to a pair.
Beside you to the east is a playground, “Roke Open Space”. June 2018 is its latest entry, and I take it to be there yet, promising nothing.
North, a few steps off, a residential building, recorded in November 2018 and not since. The building keeps no name at all. Turn east again and it is “Roke Open Space” that answers.
v16-2aff2a141c07b120.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: An unnamed service road, inside a residential area. No surface is given, no lights, no limit. The road has a place on the map and nothing else.
There is little to tell. Nothing stands beside you that the map thought worth a word.
About 25 metres to the south-east is a bus stop. Of bench, shelter or reference the map says nothing; it gives a name and stops there. The name is “Longhurst Road”.
v16-2b04510216c4ccac.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Mickleham Way, limit 20 mph, houses about you and grass to the south. Of what is here I give only some.
Where you stand, the map has a point, “Beddington–Rowdown №2”, National Grid's, noted as “Decommissioned in 2021. Most of the cable has since been removed.” East, beside you, a wood with a name.
A cable taken up beside a wood left standing. The wood is Castlehill Ruffs.
v16-2b24feb758839455.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Little Roke Road, a railway area to the south-west, and more besides. A gate stands right where you are.

All around lies “Harris Primary Academy Kenley”, at 51 Little Roke Road, a school run by Harris Federation. In October 2023, it is said, an amendment asked that a steel mesh enclosure be dropped: “replacement with a timber fence”. Its answer was “Approved”.
So one fence gave way to another, by an application, at the school run by Harris Federation.
v16-2b2b2d266d2db8eb.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: On Station Approach, 20 mph, a residential area off to the north-west. Not everything here gets a line from me.

Right beside you to the south-east is the station building, 8WX4+9C Station Approach, run by Southern, as last recorded in May 2021. It carries a short history in the map's own words: opened on 10 March 1884; the original building destroyed by fire in June 1986; the current structure opening in September 1987.
To the north, close by, is the parking, recorded last in October 2012 and named for the station: “Sanderstead Station Parking”.
v16-2b3c404ddaaaa16b.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: An unnamed footway in a retail area, and right where you stand, a crossing. Its last recording was May 2018; it crosses here still, or crossed.
Right here too, the parking: “Ikea”, run by Ikea, entered as “Ikea car park” in February 2018. You stand on both at once.
The nearest are these. The others I let go without counting. A crossing and a car park on one spot, each with its own month.
v16-2b3f893267d2f324.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Brigstock Road meets Cotford Road. Pavement on both sides, 20 mph. A retail area, a commercial area beside it to the south, a residential area to the south-east. I tell only a part.
A few steps to the north-west, an address at 1-85, and nothing else said of it, a span of numbers standing for whatever it holds.

In the same direction, just as near, a supermarket at 32 Brigstock Road. Wheelchairs can use it; it keeps “Su 11:00-17:00; Mo-Sa 06:00-23:00”. Its food hygiene rating is 5, so it is said, given in January 2025. The name over all of that is “Tesco”.
v16-2b43c28f2ef6bed9.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Stroud Green Gardens, lit at night, a pavement on one side, 20 mph. You are in a residential area, with a grass area to the south-west.

A short way south is a park, “Ashburton Playing Fields”. It went into the map in June 2017 and nothing has been added since; it is a park, or it was then. They say it is a “playing field in Woodside, London”.
The street is called gardens and the park is called fields. The grass area lies between the two names.
v16-2b627687ac91f8a0.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Lansdowne Road, with land of every kind pressed up to it: a residential area to the north, a commercial area to the south-west, an industrial area and a railway area to the east, and to the south-east a construction area, “Ruskin Square plots B-D”.
Beside you, to the south-west, a give way. To the north-west, parking, and the parking has a name too: “Ruskin Square plots E-F”.
Past those two I let things go. B to D is under construction; E to F is parking. The letters run on, along Lansdowne Road.
v16-2b750f5315a5f8f4.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: The Glade meets Lorne Gardens, 20 mph, with homes to the east.
A few steps north there is a bus stop, “Darley Close”. There was one in April 2019, when it was last written in, and the stop's entry ends there.
Gardens on one side, a glade on the other, and a stop that calls itself a close, as if the corner wanted a third name to stand on.
v16-2b825d063f87e101.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Norbury Road and Moffat Road meet at 20 mph. A speed hump lies a few steps north-east.

About 30 metres south, at 45 Norbury Road, there is a furniture shop; there was, at least, in September 2018, its final recording. Somewhere in the reckoning of what else stands between, my count goes astray, and I begin afresh.
Its name ends on an exclamation, and so does this: “Carpets & Beds Plus!”
v16-2bc0ffda2ed6be85.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Whitehorse Road, lit at night, the limit 30 mph. A residential area lies north-west of you, and a recreation ground to the east.

West, beside you, a point the map marks without saying what it is. South-west, the “Brighton Main Line”, run by Network Rail, reference “VTB1”. Then something, and something after it; I have lost the count already, and pick up the walk again without it.
The unmarked point stays unmarked. The rail goes on to the south-west, under the name “Brighton Main Line”.
v16-2bc615e9d398057a.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Here Watney Close finishes. Lit at night, 20 mph, residential, and railway land to the south-east.

Hard by, south-eastward, lies a rail, “Brighton Main Line”, run by Network Rail, with the reference “VTB2”. Then a further one, its name and reference unchanged. Is that the second, or the first again from a fresh angle? I had the number and I have dropped it.
Whatever the tally, each one says “Brighton Main Line”, and the close halts before any of them.
v16-2bcd11dd14d28526.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Limpsfield Road, concrete underfoot. A retail area here, a residential one beyond to the north-east.

Hard by on the south-east, a roof building: a roof the map counts as a building, and that is all it is granted. Hard by on the north-east, a charging station, “Shell Recharge”, run by Shell Recharge. It is its own keeper, by name at least.
The rest I let go.
v16-2be3911b9d7ec56c.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: The end of Becket Close, 20 mph. A turning circle here, as the map had it in August 2012.

To the south, beside you, “St Thomas Becket Catholic Primary School”, at Becket Close, run by St Benedict Catholic Academy Trust. Roman catholic. And to the south again, the same school in the same words, set down a second time.
Its opening is given elsewhere as 1 September 2012. The close and the school share a name; which had it first I cannot say.
v16-2c1fe6bd3443bf5f.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Mitcham Road, lit at night, 30 mph. A residential area lies to the south-west, a commercial area to the north-west, and “Croydon Cemetery” to the north-east. Of the crowd here I take the first few.
Right here, a point the map marks without saying what it is.
A few steps south-east, a bus stop. Its name carries a lane and the cemetery together: “Therapia Lane / Croydon Cemetery”.
v16-2c31d0cdd3c572af.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Brighton Road and Purley Road meet at 30 mph, a commercial area to the north.
To the south-east, at 345 Brighton Road, is a pub, “The Purley Arms”, with outdoor seating. Those who inspect kitchens gave it a 4, in October 2023.

North-west, at 328, “Pizza Hut Delivery”: pizza, takeaway only. It too was given a 4, in September 2026. In May 2022, they say, an application for “internally illuminated fascia signage” was “Approved”. And after that I had the next thing in hand, and now I have not. No matter.
The pub and the takeaway, a 4 apiece, either side of Brighton Road.
v16-2c36d6adf7c6a289.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: The end of an unnamed raceway, dirt underfoot, an industrial area beside you to the north-west.
All around is a track for motocross, or was in March 2019. Beside you on the south-west, a wood, as of April 2014.

A few steps west, “Pear Tree Farm Transfer Station”, a waste transfer station, of that April too. At 30 metres the same way, a point with no kind given, inscribed “Greater London - Surrey”, from March 2019. The raceway goes round; the line goes straight; they cross somewhere near the station.
v16-2c42ea0a37088423.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Farleigh Border meets Broom Path, dirt underfoot, farmland to the south. You stand in “Selsdon Wood”, or “Selsdon Nature Reserve”, as the reserve also goes; a wood around you and a wood a few steps east, both of September 2013.
Just south the map puts a point marked “Greater London - Surrey”. Greater London lies one side, Surrey the other; March 2019 is its date.
Farleigh Border, the path is called, and a few steps south, by the map's word, the border is.
v16-2c62b3ae7ee3e0d5.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Croham Valley Road and Manor Way meet at 20 mph, in a residential area, “Whitgift Sports Club” beside you to the north-west.

Close by to the south-west, the point National Grid keeps, “Beddington–Rowdown №2”. With it, a cable in the care of UK Power Networks, “Beddington–Rowdown 2”. More lies here than I can hold in order; I lose the count, then take up the cable again.
Its note is brief: “Decommissioned in 2021. Most of the cable has since been removed.” A manor in a road's name, and a cable that is mostly not there.
v16-2c71ff5eeadf7af0.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Watney Close, running to a dead end, lit at night, 20 mph. Residential here, and a railway area pressing in from the south-east.

Right beside you lies a rail, “Brighton Main Line”, run by Network Rail, reference “VTB2”. Steps beyond, the same again, and the same again, and once more after that: lengths of one line, each with one name and one reference.
The close ends; the “Brighton Main Line” carries on.
v16-2cb7da5311c6f635.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: This is the end of Edith Road, at 20 mph.

A few steps south, an address at Edith Road, without a number, and another at 67 Edith Road. North-east, 42a Edith Road, and about 25 metres off, 42. All four share a last date, September 2014; they are there, or were.
Of number 67, someone wrote down an application from March 2026: “Continued use of dwelling house as two self-contained units”. It was “Approved”.
One house that is two, a 42 that has an a, and an address with no number at all. The road keeps them in its last few steps.
v16-2cc83da6d63795a7.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Mayday Road, at 20 mph, a residential area to the south. Much here goes untold.

A crossing beside you on the north-west. Beside you on the north, 530 London Road, a hospital that gives its hours as “24/7” and its other name as “Mayday Hospital”. It is said that in March 2024 someone applied for “provision of two electrical transformers, associated fencing, gates and landscaping”, among other works, and that the application was “Approved”.
Its name, the one it gives first, is “Croydon University Hospital”.
v16-2cd6d14c4710dbe5.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Mitchley Avenue, lit at night, 30 mph, a residential area here and railway land to the north-west.

The “Riddlesdown Tunnel” is all around you, by the map's reckoning, and the “East Grinstead Line” runs right here, in the tunnel, under Network Rail, reference “SCU1”. Beside you to the south-west it is given again, the same in every particular.
About 55 metres west is a bus stop, bench and shelter, lit, Transport for London's, reference 53223. Its name carries a school and a station at once: “Riddlesdown School / Riddlesdown Station”.
v16-2d2c325dfed924a8.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: The track ends without a name, beside a grass area to the north-east that carries one: “Addington Reservoir”.
Beside you to the west is a substation run by UK Power Networks. On it: “Coombe Lane”. Its reference is “212236”.
A few steps south-west lie both cables: “Beddington Cable Tunnel”, which National Grid PLC runs underground in its tunnel, and “Beddington–Rowdown 2”, UK Power Networks', reference “BEDD2–ROWD4”.
About 40 metres south-east there is a gate; there was in May 2020, when it was last recorded. A reservoir by name, a grass area by the map.
v16-2d308209e515cd12.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: A nameless footway, unlit, inside “South Norwood Recreation Ground”, with railway ground to the east.
South, a few steps, is a playground, one that wheelchairs can use. Nothing further is said of it.

About 30 metres east lie “Norwood Yard and Selhurst Workshop Sidings”, a rail of Network Rail's, under the reference “NYD”. The playground near, the sidings further off, and the unlit path between them.
v16-2d4c9a12922c3b78.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: An unnamed path over grass, with a residential area to the north-east and allotments to the south-west. The park is “Heavers Meadow”, all around.
Right here is “Heavers Farm Primary School”, at 58 Dinsdale Gardens, run by London Borough of Croydon. Wheelchairs can use it. Those who inspect kitchens gave it a 5, it is said, in September 2025.

A building lies about 40 metres west; December 2017 is the last that was heard of it. At 50 metres to the south, a wetland, last set down in May 2013. A farm in the school's name, a meadow in the park's.
v16-2d9eb1ee4e049d2e.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: An unnamed footway, lit at night, and all around it “South Croydon Recreation Ground”. The park has the name; the path has none.
To the south-east, a railway area and a residential area side by side, and close on that side the “Brighton Main Line”, run by Network Rail under the reference “VTB2”.
What else is close I give up without a tally. The footway keeps to the park, and the park keeps to its name.
v16-2dbc1692211b8fbd.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Brigstock Road, lit at night, pavement on one side, 30 mph. A retail area, with a commercial area beside it to the south. The nearest pair will do; the remainder goes uncounted.
A few steps to the south, a retail building of two storeys, “Cotford Parade”. So it read in September 2018, its latest record. A parade then; a parade still, I suppose.

A few steps to the north-west, a supermarket at 32 Brigstock Road: “Tesco”. Wheelchairs can use it. Its hours are given as “Su 11:00-17:00; Mo-Sa 06:00-23:00”. In January 2025, by the word of those who inspect kitchens, its rating came to 5.
v16-2dc6068a666cd082.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Granville Gardens stops here, among houses.

Where you stand, the map marks “Norbury Brook”, run into a tunnel; that was July 2012. South-east, at your side, the brook surfaces in the record again, “Norbury Brook” once more, from April 2012, with no tunnel said.
Beside that, the park, “Norbury Park”. South-west, parking, given as of June 2012.
April, June, July: the brook entered twice, the parking once between, and the park, undated, between them on the map.
v16-2dfbc5eb55691ed8.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: The Glade meets Glade Gardens. 20 mph, homes to the north-east.
The nearest: a few steps east, a bus stop, “Glade Gardens”, reference “54552”. A few steps north, 20 The Glade, entered in October 2018. The rest I let go.
A street, a second street, and a stop, and the glade in every name.
v16-2e0084cefe3b0e94.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Fairbairn Close, 20 mph, a residential place with a railway area lying north-west of it.
Some 25 metres north-west lies a rail, “Brighton Main Line”. Network Rail runs it, and it carries a reference, “VTB2”.
That is all the close gives me: residential on one hand, the line on the other, and on the line a name that promises Brighton. The close itself promises nothing beyond its own short length.
v16-2e0900213497ef64.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Lambert's Place ends here, lit at night, and more crowds round the end of it than I can set down. A residential area lies to the south, a retail area to the north-west, and to the east a brownfield area and a railway area share the same side.
Eastward, right beside you, a fence. Beyond it, a few steps to the south-east, runs a rail. Network Rail has the running of it, and it carries a reference, “VTB2”.
The street gives up where the fence begins. The rail does not give up at all: it is the “Brighton Main Line”.
v16-2e3a8d1e7ce17609.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Newman Road, heading for a dead end, in a retail area.
A few steps south, “Booker Wholesale”, a wholesale shop. A few steps north, a building, last recorded in January 2013.

About 60 metres south-west, the tram, “London Trams (Wimbledon Branch)”, run by Transport for London, its reference “CMJ”. At about the same distance west, a platform, with a bench, a bin and a shelter, tactile paving, and wheelchairs can use it. A dead end for the road, a platform for the tram.
v16-2e46ffbe4f65535d.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: The Ridgeway, Croydon Road and Cherry Hill Gardens meet. Lit at night; 30 mph. Houses to the east; to the west, an industrial area that calls itself “iO Centre”.
Beside you to the north-west, a give way. To the south, the cable “Beddington–Rowdown 2”. That is the nearest of it, and the rest I let go.
A ridge and a cherry hill in the street names, and the cable holding to its reference: “BEDD2–ROWD4”.
v16-2e69bf7ef084ed07.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: A service road with no name, going towards Wellesley Road. You are in a retail area, commerce at the north-west.

All around you, three storeys of mall shop: “Whitgift Centre”. Wheelchairs can use it. Its hours are set down as “Mo-Sa 09:00-18:30; Su 11:00-17:00”. North, at your side, bicycle parking. I count these, lose count among the storeys, and come back out at the bicycles.
A service road, and the mall on every side of it: “Whitgift Centre”.
v16-2e86494a95e952eb.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: An unnamed footway, paving stones underfoot. Retail to the west, grass to the north, residential to the south.

Right here is a supermarket of one storey at 64 Westow Street, “Sainsbury's”, also called “Sainsbury's Upper Norwood Superstore”. Its hours are given as “Mo-Fr 08:00-21:00; Sa 07:30-21:00; Su 11:00-17:00”. Those who inspect kitchens rated it 5, they say, in December 2024.

A photo booth stands right here as well. I lose count between the booth and the shop, then find my place in the ledger. In November 2024, it is said, came an application: “T5 Sycamore  - fell to combat subsidence damage”. It was “No Objection to Proposal (OBS only)”.
v16-2e8c85c3bc8dfd71.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Enmore Road and Denmark Road cross, lit at night, pavements on both sides, 20 mph. The corner holds more than I will reckon, and I leave the rest where it lies.
A broadleaved tree, a few steps to the north-east. A few steps the other way, to the south-east, healthcare, under the only name on the corner: “Woodside Health Centre”.
A tree on one side and a health centre on the other, and the crossing keeping both at a few steps' remove.
v16-2e9c4877de674657.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Church Street, Crown Hill and Surrey Street meet, lit at night, pavement on both sides, with a retail area to the south-east. I name a part, and leave the remainder.
Right here, a point, marked and left without a kind. Right here, also, the tram, “London Trams”, run by Transport for London.
A mark with nothing to say for itself; a tram with a name and someone to run it. Between them, the corner, and the streets' names: Church Street, Crown Hill, Surrey Street.
v16-2e9d4bd93a0eb42d.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Reedham Drive meets Aveling Close, a residential area to the north-west, grass to the east.

A few steps south, “St Nicholas School”, at Reedham Drive, kept by London Borough of Croydon. Those who inspect kitchens marked it 5 in July 2026, it is said. Just north-east, the post box with “EIIR” on it and “CR8 593” for a reference.
South-west, parking at about 35 metres, and at about 50 a gate. The close, the drive, the school: all named, and the gate not.
v16-2ecab63f00aa8c1f.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Maberley Road, lit at night, with pavement on both sides and a limit of 20 mph. Grass lies off to the west.

Beside you, at 9 Maberley Road, is “Harris City Academy Crystal Palace”, run by Harris Federation. It is said its food hygiene rating was 5, given in May 2026. March 2025 brought an application, someone noted: “Installation of solar PV panels.” It was “Approved”.

To the north-east stands a bus stop with nearly the same name, “Harris City Academy”, lit at night and carrying the reference “74830”. Past these two the road holds more, and I let it keep it. The stop has the name; the school has the rest of it.
v16-2ed25649947eaef1.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Ditches Lane, 30 mph. Meadow to the south-west, farmland north-west.
All round, “Figgs Wood”, last recorded in May 2017. It was a wood then, and the map has it as one still.
A few steps south-west, a point left without a description, recorded in May 2021, bearing “Greater London - Surrey”. Surrey sits to one side of it, Greater London to the other.
The lane runs through “Figgs Wood” with the meadow at its shoulder.
v16-2eebf1f0bf2d641c.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Hayes Lane, without lamps, the limit 30 mph, houses lying north-east. More is here than these.
Right where you stand, a point bearing the words “Greater London - Surrey”: Greater London to this hand, Surrey to that. Right here as well, another point, which bears nothing.
Of the points, the lettered one gets the say. On Hayes Lane it reads “Greater London - Surrey”.
v16-2f093724247b32d8.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Bensham Manor Road, and a gate right where you stand. It has no name to give.

South-west, beside you, “St John's Congregational Church”, a place of worship; Evangelical, the map adds. Past it there is more along the road, and more again; I had a number for it and dropped it somewhere about here.
Back to what holds still: a gate, unnamed, and beside it the church with its long name, “St John's Congregational Church”.
v16-2f211eec7dd33dc8.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: An unnamed footway, and not much on it that the map will speak of.
About 30 metres to the north, they say, a “Nuthatch” was seen, in January 2023. Not on the map, which has the footway and leaves the footway without a name or a surface or a limit.
So the one thing told here is told by someone else, and told of a month long gone. The path is the map's and the “Nuthatch” is hearsay, and you stand on the first and hear of the second.
v16-2f25210fe6013ff0.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: St James's Road meets Thornhill Road. Lit at night, 30 mph. Homes to the north, commerce to the east.

South, beside you, a point the map leaves blank, and a building at 73 Oakfield Road: “Croydon & District Masonic Hall”, it says. Its kitchen, those who inspect kitchens say, was given a 4 in October 2025.

West, some 35 metres, the memorial to “C. B. Fry”, and with it a plaque the map does not hold. Point, hall, memorial, plaque; I drop the count there and pick it up again at the hall. The plaque calls him an “all-round sportsman”, and says he “was born here”.
Oakfield Road on the hall, though the corner belongs to St James's Road and Thornhill Road.
v16-2f387455b25dfb2c.model: written in a Claude Code session

paragraphs: Brighton Road, lit at night, 30 mph, with a railway area to the east.
Right here, a crossing with tactile paving; just north, traffic signals.

Some 35 metres south-east, a plaque. It reads “Erected to commemorate one hundred years of Coulsdon Station, opened October 1 1889 renamed Coulsdon & Cane Hill (Mar. 1896) then Coulsdon East (July 1923) and Coulsdon South (1 Aug. 1923)”.
I take the names in order and lose one partway, Cane Hill or East, then find it again. The plaque keeps them all, in its own order.

The rest I leave uncounted. South-west, beside you, bicycle parking.
